title: Unified UK Census Data (2021/22): harmonised small-area tables
refresh: None until the next census (2031/32). The download needs a free GeoDS registration, so it cannot be fetched automatically.
attribution: The data have been provided by the Geographic Data Service (geods.ac.uk), a Smart Data Research UK Investment: ES/Z504464/1. These were created as part of an ESRC Census data opportunity grant - ES/Z50273X/1. Contains data from: ONS, NRS, NISRA. Licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
citation: Goodwin, O. and Singleton, A. (2026) A unified dataset of UK census variables for small areas: harmonised data tables from the 2021 England, Wales, and Northern Ireland censuses and the 2022 Scotland census. Environment and Planning B: Urban Analytics and City Science.

fetch.manual: Register at https://data.geods.ac.uk/, download the Unified UK Census variable metadata and the per-table CSVs, and put them in data/raw/unified_census/ (CSVs in csv/).

caveats: Scotland's census was a year later (March 2022) than the rest of the UK's (March 2021).
Aggregated to local authorities (361 points): each authority's total sits at the weighted centre of that statistic within the authority.

excludedTables.uk007a: age — owner's rule (all bands sat on the population line)

stats.question: people who commute by underground, metro or tram
caveats: England, Wales and Northern Ireland were counted in March 2021, during a COVID-19 lockdown; Scotland in March 2022. Travel to work therefore under-counts commuting outside Scotland and over-counts working from home.

absentFrom.Northern Ireland: Northern Ireland has no underground, metro or tram system.
